entities.title: The host's browser decides the match
entities.summary: Unlike the lockstep games, Double Cross is not deterministic: the host's browser holds the hidden state (where the intel is, the traps) and decides every search, trap, punch and win.
entities.context: Traps and hidden intel must stay secret from the other players, and a physics-driven 3D game is hard to keep bit-for-bit identical across browsers.
entities.decision: The lowest slot in the match hosts. Each browser moves its own agent and sends where it is; everything else goes to the host as a request (rq_*), and the host sends back what happened (ev_*). Only the host's ev_* messages are accepted.
entities.rationale: Keeps secrets out of the other browsers and needs nothing from the relay but delivery.
consequences: If the host leaves, the match ends for everyone; the others go back to the briefing room together.
There is no high-score table: the server can't replay a match.

entities.title: Online matches use the games hub's relay
entities.summary: Double Cross has no Durable Object of its own; it sends its messages through the hub's relay at /games/multiplayer/match/{ID}, like Rally, Shatterbelt and Hivestorm.
entities.context: Players meet in one multiplayer lobby on icelander.net, which already makes matches and relays them.
entities.decision: The client connects to the relay named by ?match=ID and wraps each message as base64 inside the relay's JSON ({t: g, d, to}).
entities.rationale: One lobby for every game; nothing to run or pay for here.

entities.title: The Compatibility renderer
entities.summary: The project uses Godot's Compatibility (WebGL 2) renderer, the only one the web export supports.
entities.context: Forward+ has screen-space ambient occlusion and indirect light, but doesn't run in browsers.
entities.decision: rendering_method is gl_compatibility everywhere; the world builder turns SSAO and SSIL on only under Forward+. Only the room the player is in casts shadows.
entities.rationale: One look on every platform, and a frame rate browsers can hold.
